findings.reason: Verified: the new action calls tu.save! without setting notifications_reason_id. TopicUser.change sets it to user_changed (topic_user.rb:87-90), and auto_track and TrackedTopicsUpdater both overwrite rows whose reason is nil, so a mute from the email can be silently undone and no MessageBus push is sent.
Verified: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when the logged-in user has no row for the topic (for example a forwarded link), and tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError, which gives a 500.

Correct: a GET with no token or confirmation changes state, so it can be triggered cross-site, and each reload steps the level down again (watching to regular to muted), so the action is not idempotent.

Verified: unsubscribe is in ensure_logged_in, and for a non-JSON GET the NotLoggedIn rescue redirects to "/" with no return path, so a logged-out user who clicks the email link lands on the homepage and nothing is unsubscribed.
The finding admits it did not confirm that in-app navigation reaches this route; email links open as full page loads that hit the server action, so the in-app case is plausible but unverified.

Correct: when the level was above regular the controller only drops it to regular, where mentions and replies still notify the user, so "You will stop receiving notifications" overstates what happens; this is a minor UX/wording issue.
Correct: no controller spec covers TopicsController#unsubscribe, and the message builder spec only passes unsubscribe_url without checking that the link appears in the email.
The misspelling stopNotificiationsText is real and is repeated in the template; it is a naming issue only.
